scenes.say: An octopus has three hearts. And it needs every one.
scenes.visual: Octopus outline draws on; three yellow hearts appear inside the mantle on @three, numbered 1-2-3, then beat.

scenes.say: The reason is its blood. It's blue, because it carries oxygen with copper instead of iron.
scenes.visual: Two drops side by side: octopus drop (yellow) lands on @blue, Cu label on @copper; our drop with Fe label on @iron.

scenes.say: Copper blood holds less oxygen than ours, so it has to be pumped harder.
scenes.visual: Two bars, oxygen per drop: ours long, octopus short on @less. Pressure gauge needle swings up on @harder.

scenes.say: So two hearts have just one job: pushing blood through the gills.
scenes.visual: Two feathery gills, a small heart at the base of each on @two; flow arrows run up through the gills on @gills.

scenes.say: That leaves the pressure low. So a third heart pumps it out to the whole body.
scenes.visual: Circuit: gills at the sides feed a large yellow heart in the middle on @third; dashed flow down to a BODY box on @body.

scenes.say: Here's the strange part. When an octopus swims, that main heart stops.
scenes.visual: Octopus drawn swimming sideways, heart beating, pulse trace running; on @stops the heart freezes and the trace goes flat.

scenes.say: So swimming wears it out fast. An octopus would much rather crawl.
scenes.visual: Sea floor line; octopus crawling along it, all three hearts beating. SWIM 2 OF 3 on @fast, CRAWL 3 OF 3 on @crawl.

scenes.say: Three hearts. Blue blood. Follow for more.
scenes.visual: Three hearts in a row drawn on one by one, beating; FOLLOW typed underneath.
